newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS aims for cargo alliance with Canada partner.
newsitem.headline: SAS aims for cargo alliance with Canada partner.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said on Thursday that future cooperation with its new partner Air Canada would probably resemble cooperation with the cargo units of Lufthansa and United.
Air Canada and SAS announced last week they had agreed to develop a comprehensive air travel alliance that may include code-sharing.
"We, of course, will develop the cargo side as well," SAS Cargo marketing manager Gunilla Emthen-Eckerstrom told Reuters.
"It's probably coming -- something like what we have with Lufthansa and United."
SAS Cargo and Lufthansa Cargo have merged handling operations and facilities at some destinations, increased collaboration on sales on smaller markets and coordinated freight systems.
The cargo divisions of SAS and Air Canada had not yet contacted each other, Emthen-Eckerstrom said.
"It usually happens a few months later," she said.
Air Canada and SAS said the pact would further strengthen their respective alliances with UAL Corp's United Airlines and Deutsche Lufthansa AG.
Provisions in the alliance, which will take effect in 1997, cover such areas such as reciprocal participation in frequent flyer programs and schedule coordination.
